name: Detroit
operatingHours: QLINE streetcar (Woodward Ave) runs Mon–Sat 8:00 AM–midnight and Sun 8:00 AM–9:00 PM, every ~15 min. The People Mover downtown loop runs Mon–Fri 6:30 AM–midnight, Sat 10:00 AM–midnight and Sun 10:00 AM–10:00 PM, every ~5 min (longer hours on big event nights). No overnight rail service.
fareInfo: Both the QLINE and the Detroit People Mover are free to ride in 2026 (sponsor-funded); just board. DDOT and SMART buses (not on this map) cost ~$2, payable with the Dart app or cash; the SMART 261 FAST Michigan bus to the airport costs the same.

sights.name: Motown Museum (Hitsville U.S.A.)
sights.note: The modest West Grand Boulevard house where Berry Gordy ran Motown Records, with the original Studio A; guided tours are paused for a major expansion and are due back in spring 2027.
sights.hours: Guided tours paused (Jan 2026–spring 2027); campus store and new Esther Gordy Edwards Centre open Wed–Sun ~10 AM–6 PM

sights.name: Detroit Institute of Arts
sights.note: One of America's great encyclopedic art museums, best known for Diego Rivera's floor-to-ceiling Detroit Industry murals in the central court.
sights.hours: Tue–Thu 9 AM–4 PM, Fri 9 AM–9 PM, Sat–Sun 10 AM–5 PM; closed Mon

sights.name: Guardian Building
sights.note: A 1929 Art Deco skyscraper whose vaulted lobby is a riot of Pewabic tile, orange brick and stained glass; free to walk in and look up.
sights.hours: Lobby open ~weekdays 8 AM–6 PM, shorter Sat; free

sights.name: Ford Piquette Avenue Plant
sights.note: The brick factory where Henry Ford built the first Model T, now a museum of early cars kept on the original creaky wooden floors.

sights.name: Comerica Park
sights.note: Home of the Detroit Tigers, with a carousel, a Ferris wheel of baseballs and giant tiger statues around a ballpark facing the downtown skyline.
sights.hours: Tigers home games Apr–Sep (Oct if in the playoffs)

sights.name: Belle Isle Park
sights.note: A 982-acre island park in the Detroit River, laid out by Olmsted, with a conservatory, aquarium, beach, fountain and views of the skyline and Canada.
sights.hours: Daily 5 AM–10 PM; free on foot or bike, Michigan Recreation Passport needed for cars

sights.name: Eastern Market
sights.note: One of the oldest public markets in the US, where farmers, butchers and flower sellers fill the open sheds and the surrounding streets are covered in murals.
sights.hours: Saturday market 6 AM–2 PM year-round; Sunday and Tuesday markets in summer; shops open most days

sights.name: Detroit RiverWalk
sights.note: A waterfront promenade running east from Hart Plaza past the Renaissance Center to parks, gardens and a carousel, looking straight across at Windsor, Canada.

sights.name: Fox Theatre
sights.note: A lavish 1928 movie palace with a gilded, vaguely Asian-Egyptian interior that now hosts concerts, Broadway tours and holiday shows.
sights.hours: Open for performances; check the show calendar

sights.name: Ford Field
sights.note: The Detroit Lions' domed stadium, built around an old Hudson's warehouse whose brick wall forms one side of the concourse.
sights.hours: Lions home games Sep–Jan; concerts and events year-round

sights.name: Greektown
sights.note: A short stretch of Monroe Street lined with Greek tavernas, bakeries and bars next to the Hollywood Casino, lively late into the night.

sights.name: Detroit Historical Museum
sights.note: The city's story in walk-through exhibits, from a recreated cobblestone street of old Detroit to a working auto assembly line and the Motor City music era.
sights.hours: Wed–Sat 10 AM–5 PM, Sun 1–5 PM; closed Mon–Tue

sights.name: The Heidelberg Project
sights.note: A long-running outdoor art installation on the east side where houses and lots are covered in polka dots, found objects and painted clocks; some pieces have been removed as the project evolves.

sights.name: Little Caesars Arena
sights.note: The arena of the Red Wings and Pistons, with a glass-roofed indoor street of shops and restaurants that is open on event days.
sights.hours: NHL and NBA seasons Oct–Apr; concerts year-round

sights.name: Michigan Central Station
sights.note: The towering Beaux-Arts rail terminal in Corktown, long a symbol of decline, reopened by Ford in 2024 with its vaulted waiting hall and arcade restored.
sights.hours: Public lobby open daily 8 AM–5 PM; free (guided tours sold separately)

sights.name: Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History
sights.note: A large museum of African American history whose core exhibit walks visitors from West Africa through the Middle Passage to Detroit's own civil rights era.
sights.hours: Tue–Wed and Fri–Sun 9 AM–5 PM, Thu 9 AM–7 PM; closed Mon

sights.name: Campus Martius Park
sights.note: The downtown square at the heart of Woodward Ave, with a sand beach and food stalls in summer and an ice rink and giant tree in winter.

sights.name: Fisher Building
sights.note: A 1928 New Center tower with a three-storey arcade of painted ceilings, marble and bronze, often called Detroit's largest art object; a short walk from the Amtrak station.
sights.hours: Arcade open ~daily during business hours; free (Fisher Theatre shows separate)

railStations.name: Detroit Amtrak Station
railStations.note: Small Amtrak station in New Center at Woodward and Baltimore. Wolverine trains run 3 times a day each way to Chicago (~5.5 h) and to Pontiac. The QLINE's Baltimore Street stop is right outside, ~15 min to downtown. Not the grand Michigan Central Station in Corktown, which no longer has trains.
railStations.hours: Waiting room ~6:00 AM–~11:30 PM, around train times; 3 departures each way daily

airports.name: Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport
airports.transitNote: No rail link and not on this map. SMART's 261 FAST Michigan bus (~$2) runs from the McNamara and Evans terminals along Michigan Ave to downtown (Rosa Parks Transit Center) in ~45–60 min, every ~30 min. A taxi or rideshare takes ~25–30 min (~$45–60).
airports.hours: 261 bus: first ~5:00 AM, last ~midnight; check SMART times
